99UENUM()
100enum class ELumenRayLightingModeOverride : uint8
101{
102 /* Use the project default method */
103 Default UMETA(DisplayName = "Project Default"),
104 /* Use Lumen Surface Cache for ray hit lighting. This method gives the best GI and reflection performance, but quality will be limited by how well surface cache represents given scene. */
105 SurfaceCache UMETA(DisplayName = "Surface Cache"),
106 /* Calculate lighting at a hit point for reflections. This will improve reflection quality, but increases GPU cost, as full material needs to be evaluated and shadow rays traced. Lumen Surface Cache will still be used for GI and secondary bounces, including GI seen in reflections. */
107 HitLightingForReflections UMETA(DisplayName = "Hit Lighting for Reflections"),
108 /* Calculate lighting at a hit point for GI and reflections. This will improve both GI and reflection quality, but greatly increases GPU cost, as full material and lighting will be evaluated at every hit point. Lumen Surface Cache will still be used for secondary bounces. */
109 HitLighting UMETA(DisplayName = "Hit Lighting"),
110};

2636 // Adds an Blendable (implements IBlendableInterface) to the array of Blendables (if it doesn't exist) and update the weight
2637 // @param InBlendableObject silently ignores if no object is referenced
2638 // @param 0..1 InWeight, values outside of the range get clampled later in the pipeline
2639 void AddBlendable(TScriptInterface<IBlendableInterface> InBlendableObject, float InWeight)
2640 {
2641 // update weight, if the Blendable is already in the array
2642 if(UObject* Object = InBlendableObject.GetObject())
2643 {
2644 for (int32 i = 0, count = WeightedBlendables.Array.Num(); i < count; ++i)
2645 {
2646 if (WeightedBlendables.Array[i].Object == Object)
2647 {
2648 WeightedBlendables.Array[i].Weight = InWeight;
2649 // We assumes we only have one
2650 return;
2651 }
2652 }
2653
2654 // add in the end
2655 WeightedBlendables.Array.Add(FWeightedBlendable(InWeight, Object));
2656 }
2657 }
2658
2659 // removes one or multiple blendables from the array
2660 void RemoveBlendable(TScriptInterface<IBlendableInterface> InBlendableObject)
2661 {
2662 if(UObject* Object = InBlendableObject.GetObject())
2663 {
2664 for (int32 i = 0, count = WeightedBlendables.Array.Num(); i < count; ++i)
2665 {
2666 if (WeightedBlendables.Array[i].Object == Object)
2667 {
2668 // this might remove multiple
2669 WeightedBlendables.Array.RemoveAt(i);
2670 --i;
2671 --count;
2672 }
2673 }
2674 }
2675 }
